auditAreas.notes: Traced per payload type. create_execution is idempotent through the CommandInbox because the acceptance request extends the context schema that carries idempotencyKey. submit_input carries no idempotency key. The metadata effect is an injected callback with no shipped implementation, and no file scanned by CP190-P21 (apps/ and packages/, excluding the relay package, tests and declarations) builds the relay host adapter. The relay receipt layer adds no idempotency beyond the command identifier and only in-memory receipt repositories ship.

auditAreas.area: HPKE AAD, recipient, replay and expiry

The provider path creates and restricts its parent directory to 0700 before the database and its sidecars exist, so there is no supported traversal path. The adapter-owned pi-durable directory is the conditional case.

findings.title: The relay host processor applies no authentication of its own to metadata-only commands
findings.releaseImpact: Does not block the current release. The Control Plane ships the transport and validation layer only: no file scanned by CP190-P21 (apps/ and packages/, excluding the relay package, tests and declarations) builds the relay host adapter or the metadata processor, the only relay client implementation is a test fake, and the approve, deny, cancel, resume and status effects are injected callbacks with no shipped implementation. What remains is that the processor offers no defence in depth of its own, so a claim that the Control Plane verifies the metadata transport cannot be made.
findings.routedTo: W1 (packages/remote-control-relay) with the Agent HQ product relay owner
findings.regression: The processor must not be able to accept a metadata command that its caller has not authenticated, and a composition must refuse to start a relay adapter whose client does not assert authentication. Regression test: a metadata command with no authenticated-transport provenance is rejected by the processor, and the composition fails closed when the supplied client declares no authentication.
findings.reachabilityClass: Reachable only after an operator configures the optional component; the component ships disabled or is not composed by default.
findings.reachabilityNote: Traced end to end: the only consumer of a metadata command is RemoteControlHostAdapter.#pollOnce (packages/remote-control-relay/src/adapter.ts:154-173), which is itself an injected option of the Local and Hosted compositions (apps/local-control-plane/src/composition.ts:249-250,508-512; apps/hosted-control-plane/src/composition.ts:220-223,371-375) and is reported as 'disabled' when absent (:152, :164). No file scanned by CP190-P21 (apps/ and packages/, excluding the relay package, tests and declarations) constructs RelayMetadataCommandProcessor or RemoteControlHostAdapter, and the only OutboundOpaqueRelayClient implementation is the test fake FakeOpaqueRelay (packages/remote-control-relay/src/relay.ts:45). The metadata effect callback is injected (packages/remote-control-relay/src/relay.ts:376-379), so the Control Plane ships no approve, deny or cancel effect at all: those names are schema operations, not shipped behaviour. An integrator must supply the relay client, the effect and the adapter. **No deployed attacker-controlled ingress exists and no deployed unauthenticated approval path is claimed.** The residual is that the processor adds no provenance check of its own and relies on its caller having authenticated the transport, which docs/remote-control-relay.md assigns to the concrete relay client.
findings.counterevidence: docs/remote-control-relay.md states that metadata-only operations use a separate strict, authenticated command schema and that authentication of that metadata transport remains the responsibility of the concrete relay client. The obligation is documented and delegated, so this is a contract and defence-in-depth gap rather than a deployed unauthenticated-approval path.

findings.title: The relay receipt layer adds no idempotency beyond the command identifier, and only in-memory receipt repositories ship
findings.releaseImpact: Does not block the current release. The durable idempotency guarantee for create_execution comes from the CommandInbox, not from the relay receipt, and the metadata effect is an injected callback whose own idempotency is outside the Control Plane.
findings.regression: Bind the effect and its receipt atomically, or bind the receipt to a stable effect key that the injected callback also uses. Do not move the receipt before the effect. Regression test: a receipt-store write that fails must leave the effect unapplied; a receipt and its effect must be indivisible; and a redelivery after a restart must be rejected as a duplicate by the durable receipt.
findings.reachabilityClass: Reachable only after an operator configures the optional component; the component ships disabled or is not composed by default.
findings.reachabilityNote: Traced per payload type. create_execution: the relay parses ExecutionAcceptanceRequestSchema (packages/remote-control-relay/src/execution.ts:209-223,260-268), which extends CommandContextSchema and therefore carries the caller's idempotencyKey (packages/contracts/src/control-api.ts:45,668); ExecutionAcceptanceService then admits it through the CommandInbox (apps/control-api/src/executions/execution-acceptance.service.ts:51,58; packages/domain/src/command-inbox.ts:53-58,684-705), so a redelivery of the same command is deduped there. submit_input: RelaySubmitInputRequestSchema carries no idempotency key at all (packages/remote-control-relay/src/execution.ts:38-52), so any dedupe must come from the interaction domain. Metadata operations: the effect is an injected callback (packages/remote-control-relay/src/relay.ts:376-379) with no shipped implementation. The effect-before-receipt order is correct and must not be inverted; the defect is that the two writes are not atomic and that only in-memory receipt repositories ship (packages/remote-control-relay/src/relay.ts:227,343; packages/remote-control-relay/src/execution.ts:135), while docs/remote-control-relay.md already records the durable repository as a composition requirement.
findings.counterevidence: create_execution goes through ExecutionAcceptanceService and the CommandInbox idempotency key, so it is not duplicated by the callback ordering. The processor offers no cross-commandId idempotency, but the commandId is a relay-chosen identifier and the effect's own idempotency is the injected callback's property.

findings.title: The direct-local runtime path never consults a LocalProjectGrant, and the production discovery state is a hard-coded constant
findings.releaseImpact: Blocks the Local filesystem/project acceptance claim: the discovery projection reports a grant state that no authority issued, and the direct-local working directory is bounded by operator configuration rather than by a grant.
findings.routedTo: W1 (runtime composition and adapter boundary) with the Agent HQ desktop grant owner
findings.regression: The direct-local driver must require a current grant, and every path must be contained against a canonical grant root after symlink resolution. Regression test: a direct-local dispatch with a revoked or absent grant is rejected; a symlinked path that escapes the grant root is rejected; and the direct-local working directory is derived from the grant rather than from operator configuration alone.
findings.reachabilityClass: Reachable in a shipped profile today, subject to the preconditions stated in the finding.
findings.reachabilityNote: Traced for the actual managed-Pi driver. ManagedPiDriver (packages/managed-pi-adapter/src/index.ts:322) parses the execution plan, enforces the runtime version range and the capability evaluation, and forwards to the client; it contains no grant reference and no path check. The child then runs with its working directory set to a per-attempt directory under the data directory (apps/local-control-plane/src/managed-pi-runtime.ts:66; packages/managed-pi-adapter/src/process-client.ts:288-298), created 0700 with the system prompt written 0600. The composed spawn policy names only allowedExecutables (apps/local-control-plane/src/index.ts:300), and NodeProcessSpawnPolicy documents absent dimensions as unconstrained (packages/deployment/src/process-runtime.ts:10), so the working-directory dimension is unconstrained by policy. The ACP path differs: the child runs in the operator-configured absolute CONTROL_PLANE_CODEX_ACP_CWD and the policy mirrors that directory (apps/local-control-plane/src/installed-acp-runtime.ts:88-95), with absolute-path validation as the only constraint. The gateway path is the only one that checks a grant (packages/managed-pi-adapter/src/managed-pi-gateway-driver.ts:108-120; packages/acp-adapter/src/acp-gateway-driver.ts:127-139), and the only production writer of the grant state is a hard-coded constant (apps/runtime-gateway/src/runtime-inventory-ingestion.ts:387) consumed at apps/workflow-worker/src/runtime-attempt-router.ts:179-184. Because the grant carries no path semantics, there is no grant-scoped project root for STA-L42-10 to attach to, and the Control Plane mediates no filesystem operation on the harness's behalf, so the residual Control Plane risk is a dispatch-authority and acceptance gap while the ambient-access denial remains a desktop-host obligation outside this repository.
findings.counterevidence: None offered. The citation error in the previous revision is corrected here: the managed-Pi direct driver is packages/managed-pi-adapter/src/index.ts:322 (export class ManagedPiDriver), not a separate managed-pi-driver.ts module, which does not exist. packages/acp-adapter/src/acp-driver-execution.ts does exist and holds no grant reference.

findings.title: The credential-vault returned-value screen does not descend into Error, Map, Set or byte containers
findings.releaseImpact: No deployed credential leakage is claimed or demonstrated. The one composed leased path normalizes the callback result before it is screened, and the two callers that return a raw result are not composed into any application.
findings.regression: The returned-value screen must descend into Error message, stack and cause, Map, Set, Buffer and typed arrays, or reject a non-plain result. Regression test: a leased callback that returns new Error(secret) must raise SECRET_EGRESS_BLOCKED; a leased callback that throws must still surface the bounded PROVIDER_OPERATION_FAILED code; and the model-selection normalizer must continue to reject a non-plain carrier.
findings.reachabilityClass: A library-level contract gap. No composed path in this repository reaches it, so no deployed behaviour is claimed.
findings.reachabilityNote: Bounded to the returned value of a leased callback. packages/credential-vault/src/vault.ts:456-467 screens the value the callback returns with containsSecret, and containsSecret (:550-557) walks own enumerable string-keyed properties only, so a returned Error, Map, Set or byte container carrying the secret is not detected. Ordinary thrown errors are already sanitized: the catch at :462-466 converts any non-CredentialVaultError throw into PROVIDER_OPERATION_FAILED. The composed leased path is protected by a second control: the model-selection service returns safeCredentialResult(await operation(secret)) (packages/model-gateway/src/selection-service.ts:269), and safeCredentialResult (:341-380) rejects any object whose prototype is not Object.prototype or null, rejects symbol keys, rejects sparse arrays and rejects cycles, so a non-plain carrier cannot survive it. The two callers that return the raw result are the credential broker (packages/credential-vault/src/tool-broker.ts:91-99) and the MCP adapter (packages/tool-execution/src/mcp-adapter.ts:257-277, which reduces thrown transport errors to a bounded code but returns the invoke output raw); neither is composed into any application, and no application composes a VaultToolCredentialBroker. The composed profiles also do not lease: the Control API vault composes no policy decision point (apps/control-api/src/cloud-composition.ts:100-104), so leases deny before a secret is resolved (packages/credential-vault/src/vault.ts:326-332).
findings.counterevidence: The previous revision implied a deployed credential-leakage path. It does not: thrown errors are sanitized, the Control API vault denies leases without a policy decision point, and the demonstrated case is a library contract gap in the returned-value screen only.

findings.reachabilityNote: Present in the shipped Local profile. The default bind is loopback (apps/local-control-plane/src/index.ts:82-88), the bearer token is a 0600 file in a 0700 directory (apps/control-api/src/auth/private-api-authentication.ts:14-43) and the caller must be svc_agent-hq, so a bearer holder is the trusted local product. findings.title: SQLite WAL and SHM sidecars keep the pre-restriction file mode inside an owner-only parent directory
findings.releaseImpact: No cross-UID readability is demonstrated and none is claimed. The parent data directory is created and restricted to 0700 before the database and its sidecars exist, so there is no supported traversal path in the provider.
findings.regression: Restrict the sidecar files to owner-only, so the file mode does not depend on the parent directory mode. Regression test: after opening a provider in a 0755 directory the -wal and -shm files must be mode 0600.
findings.reachabilityClass: A hardening gap. The described attack is not demonstrated as reachable; the stated control prevents it in the current configuration.
findings.reachabilityNote: packages/sqlite-persistence/src/provider.ts:209-210 creates the parent directory and chmods it to 0700 before the database is opened at :211 and before the WAL pragma at :216, and :221 then restricts the main file to 0600. The sidecars keep the pre-restriction mode, but another UID cannot traverse the 0700 parent, and no supported path defeats that control. The residual is defence in depth: the sidecar files are not owner-only, so a later relaxation of the directory mode, a copy of a sidecar on its own, or a backup that captures a sidecar would expose recent writes that the 0600 main file would have protected. The adapter-owned directory case is reported separately as CP190-F29.
findings.counterevidence: The previous revision implied a cross-UID read. The parent directory is 0700 before any file is created, so the sidecar mode is a defense-in-depth gap only.

findings.title: The Control Plane repository ships a RuntimeNode credential issuer CLI
findings.releaseImpact: Credential-class separation: issuer signing code is co-located with the verifier-only gateway's repository and image build context. That an issuer private key is present on Control Plane infrastructure is not shown by the source and is an evidence gap. Rotation and credential-class separation acceptance stay open.
findings.regression: Proposed evidence request, not a gate: inspect the built image manifest for the issuer CLI and any issuer key path without reading key material. If the image carries the issuer CLI, move issuance to a separate operator surface and keep the gateway verifier-only.
findings.reachabilityClass: Reachable only after an operator configures the optional component; the component ships disabled or is not composed by default.
findings.reachabilityNote: Source shows: scripts/runtime-node-identity-admin.mjs signs credentials with an Ed25519 private key read from an operator-supplied absolute path (--issuer-private-key; the file must be a private regular file owned by the invoking user), and both infrastructure/containers/Dockerfile and Dockerfile.hosted copy scripts/ into the build context (Dockerfile:7, Dockerfile.hosted:7 and :94). docs/runtime-node-identity-operations.md states that key registration and credential issuance are deliberately offline operator actions and that the issuer private half is kept offline or in the operator's protected key service; only the public PEM belongs on the gateway. Source does not show: where any issuer private key is stored, or that one exists on Control Plane infrastructure. That placement is an evidence gap. No key material was read.
findings.evidenceGap: Deployed placement of the issuer private key is not established by the repository.

findings.title: The Hosted server profile composes no credential vault and the host-secure handle provider has no resolver
findings.releaseImpact: The self-hosted server profile has no dynamic credential lifecycle and no OS-secure handle path. STA-L15-01, STA-L40-11 and STA-L40-14 acceptance stay open.
findings.routedTo: W1 (apps/hosted-control-plane composition) and the desktop owner for the OS resolver
findings.regression: Compose the vault for the hosted server profile and wire a concrete host-secure resolver for packaged Local. Regression test: a hosted server composition must resolve a credential lifecycle, and a packaged Local profile must resolve an opaque handle.
findings.reachabilityClass: Reachable only after an operator configures the optional component; the component ships disabled or is not composed by default.

findings.title: The spawn policy check is not pinned to the executed path
findings.releaseImpact: A symlink swap between the allowlist check and the spawn can launch an unlisted executable. STA-L69-01 and STA-L77-01 acceptance stay open.
findings.regression: Execute the resolved canonical path and re-verify the device and inode identity, as the secrets provider already does. Regression test: swapping the allowlisted executable for a symlink after the check must not launch the replacement.
findings.reachabilityClass: A hardening gap. The described attack is not demonstrated as reachable; the stated control prevents it in the current configuration.
findings.reachabilityNote: The check and the spawn are two separate steps, so a symlink swap in the window between them could launch an unlisted executable. The window is narrow, it requires local write access to the executable path, and no supported path widens it, so this is defence in depth rather than a demonstrated privilege gain.

findings.title: The exported direct-local ACP runtime factory applies no spawn policy by default
findings.releaseImpact: An embedder can start an arbitrary absolute executable at an arbitrary absolute working directory. STA-L27-03 and STA-L77-01 acceptance stay open for embedders.
findings.regression: Require an explicit spawn policy in the exported factory. Regression test: creating the factory without a spawn policy must fail closed.
findings.reachabilityClass: Reachable only after an operator configures the optional component; the component ships disabled or is not composed by default.

findings.title: Marketplace registry egress accepts any HTTPS URL with no metadata-range denial
findings.releaseImpact: A misconfigured registry base URL can reach a metadata endpoint. STA-L31-02 and STA-L33-01 acceptance stay open.
findings.regression: Deny the link-local and metadata ranges on the registry fetch path. Regression test: a registry base URL resolving to 169.254.169.254 must be refused.
findings.reachabilityClass: Reachable only after an operator configures the optional component; the component ships disabled or is not composed by default.

findings.title: The Restate interaction response handler resolves by name without a responding-principal check
findings.releaseImpact: An approval or input delivered over the workflow ingress is not re-checked against the authorized principal set on that path. STA-L66-01 and STA-L42-11 acceptance stay open.
findings.regression: Re-check the responding principal against the interaction allowed principal set before resolving. Regression test: a response from a principal outside allowedPrincipalIds must be rejected.
findings.reachabilityClass: Reachable only after an operator configures the optional component; the component ships disabled or is not composed by default.

findings.title: Tool rate-limit events are only deleted for the tuple being checked
findings.releaseImpact: Rows for abandoned principal, tool or operation tuples accumulate without bound. Retention acceptance stays open.
findings.regression: Sweep expired tool rate-limit rows in the retention pass. Regression test: the retention sweep must remove expired tool_rate_limit_events rows for a tuple that is never called again.
findings.reachabilityClass: Reachable in a shipped profile today, subject to the preconditions stated in the finding.

findings.title: Staging and production share one R2 bucket and are separated by a key prefix in source; whether their credentials are distinct is not shown
findings.releaseImpact: Environment separation of object keys rests on a prefix, which is visible in source. Whether staging and production hold distinct bucket-scoped credentials is not shown by the source and is an evidence gap. STA-L31-01, STA-L31-02 and STA-L40-11 acceptance stay open.
findings.regression: Proposed evidence request, not a gate: the operations owner states whether staging and production credentials are distinct. If they are shared, provision distinct bucket-scoped credentials and add a cross-environment read-denied test.
findings.reachabilityClass: Reachable only after an operator configures the optional component; the component ships disabled or is not composed by default.
findings.reachabilityNote: Source shows: .railway/railway.ts:82-89 and :133-139 declare R2_BUCKET 'ctrl-plane' for both environments and add R2_PREFIX 'staging/' only when not production, and packages/object-store/src/index.ts:140-142 applies the prefix to every address. R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID and R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY are declared with preserve() in both, meaning the value is kept in Railway and not set by source. Source does not show: whether the preserved values or their bucket scopes are shared or distinct between environments. Matching variable names are not evidence of matching values. That is an evidence gap. No credential value was read.
findings.evidenceGap: Whether staging and production R2 credentials are distinct in value or scope is not established by the repository.

findings.title: The pi-durable adapter creates its own data directory without an owner-only mode
findings.releaseImpact: No cross-UID read is demonstrated and none is claimed. In the composed managed-cloud path an ancestor directory is created owner-only, which blocks traversal today. The control that the adapter relies on is therefore owned by a different component than the data.
findings.reachabilityClass: A hardening gap. The described attack is not demonstrated as reachable; a stated control prevents it in the current configuration.
findings.reachabilityNote: packages/pi-durable-adapter/src/journal.ts:31 and packages/pi-durable-adapter/src/lease.ts:20 create their directories with mkdirSync(..., { recursive: true }) and no mode, so the directory takes the process umask default, and the database file is never chmod'ed. apps/control-api/src/pi-durable/node-composition.ts:89 does the same for the admission database. In the composed managed-cloud path the ancestor is created owner-only (apps/control-api/src/models/production-model-composition.ts:230), which blocks traversal, so the guarantee is inherited from an unrelated composition rather than enforced by the component that owns the data. Any other wiring would place a 0644 database in a 0755 directory, which is a supported traversal path; no such wiring ships.
findings.counterevidence: No counterevidence was offered. The finding is bounded by the inherited ancestor mode and by the absence of any wiring that defeats it.
findings.routedTo: W1 (packages/pi-durable-adapter and the apps/control-api pi-durable composition)
findings.regression: The adapter must create its own directory owner-only and restrict the database file, rather than inheriting the guarantee from an ancestor. Regression test: construct the adapter with a fresh directory under a 0755 parent and assert the created directory is 0700 and the database file is 0600.

calibration.rule: A finding states what the code does and what that makes reachable. It never asserts a deployed impact that the counterevidence contradicts.

packages/remote-control-relay/src/relay.ts:45 (only relay client implementation is a test fake)

Ordinary thrown errors are sanitized and the Control API vault denies leases without a policy decision point, so this is a bounded library callback-result egress contract gap and not a demonstrated deployed credential leakage.

probeInterpretations: CP190-P05 now asserts both halves of the boundary: a thrown error is sanitized to PROVIDER_OPERATION_FAILED, and a returned Error carrier is not screened.
CP190-P09 and CP190-P10 now read packages/managed-pi-adapter/src/index.ts and fail loudly when the file is missing or empty, so a nonexistent path can never be reported as a missing grant check.
CP190-P13 now records both the mitigating parent-directory control and the non-owner-only sidecar mode, and classifies the result as defense in depth.
CP190-P02, CP190-P03 and CP190-P04 now state the reachability bound and the documented delegation, and no longer imply a deployed unauthenticated approval path or a universal duplicate-effect path.

CP190-P21 classifies the relay path: it scans apps/ and packages/ recursively (outside the relay package, tests and declarations), finds no construction of the relay host adapter or the metadata processor and no call to createRelayExecutionMetadataCommandProcessor, and shows that the only relay client is a test fake and that the metadata effect is injected, so the finding is a contract and defence-in-depth gap rather than a deployed approval path.

CP190-P22 classifies the relay idempotency: it proves that the acceptance request carries the caller's idempotency key while submit_input carries none, so the durable guarantee is the CommandInbox's, not the receipt's.

CP190-P23 classifies the vault egress gap: it proves that the composed model-selection path normalizes the leased result and rejects a non-plain carrier, so only the uncomposed raw-result callers can reach the screen with an exotic container.

CP190-P24 classifies the direct-local path: it proves that the managed-Pi driver checks no grant and that the composed spawn policy leaves the working directory unconstrained, so the bound is operator configuration.
CP190-P25 splits the SQLite observation: it proves that the provider creates an owner-only parent before any file exists, and that the pi-durable adapter creates its own directory without a mode.

rounds.method: Each finding was traced from its entrypoint through the authority and effect path to the point where a control is applied, and each probe was re-read as a synthetic demonstration rather than as deployed behaviour.
changes: F-01: the reachability statement now names the traced path and states that the Control Plane ships no metadata effect implementation at all; the earlier wording implied a live approve, deny or cancel effect that the package does not contain.

F-02: the reachability statement now separates create_execution, which is idempotent through the CommandInbox because the acceptance request extends the context schema that carries idempotencyKey, from submit_input, whose schema carries no idempotency key at all.

F-03: the reachability statement now traces the actual managed-Pi driver and shows that the child working directory is a per-attempt directory under the data directory, that the spawn policy leaves the working-directory dimension unconstrained, and that the ACP path instead uses an operator-configured absolute directory.

F-04: the reachability statement now names the positive control that the earlier revision missed, safeCredentialResult in the model-selection service, which rejects a non-plain carrier before the vault screen sees it, and names the two uncomposed raw-result callers.
F-09: split. The provider limb stays a defence-in-depth observation with no traversal path, and the adapter-owned directory is reported separately as CP190-F29 with the conditional path stated.
CP190-F29 added: the pi-durable adapter creates its own directory without an owner-only mode, so its protection is inherited from an ancestor rather than enforced locally.
Five static reachability probes added: CP190-P21 to CP190-P25.

targetedEvidenceQuestions.question: Which profile, if any, is expected to lease a connector credential in the release candidate, and what result shapes can a tool executor return from a leased callback?
targetedEvidenceQuestions.why: The returned-value screen only matters once a profile composes a policy decision point. The answer sets whether the egress contract is a release blocker or a library hardening item.
targetedEvidenceQuestions.owner: W1 (profile compositions) with the credential-vault owner

targetedEvidenceQuestions.question: Does any supported deployment capture the SQLite -wal or -shm sidecar independently of the database file, and can the data directory mode be relaxed by configuration?
targetedEvidenceQuestions.why: The parent directory is 0700 before creation, so the sidecar mode is defense in depth. It becomes material only if a backup or a configuration change separates a sidecar from its parent.

targetedEvidenceQuestions.question: Which concrete relay client will be configured for a release profile, and how does that client authenticate the transport and the store it reads from?
targetedEvidenceQuestions.why: The documented delegation is only as strong as the concrete client. Until one is named, the host processor's lack of its own check is a defence-in-depth gap and not a deployed path.
targetedEvidenceQuestions.owner: W1 with the Agent HQ product relay owner

targetedEvidenceQuestions.question: Does the injected metadata accept callback provide its own idempotency for approve, deny, cancel and resume, and is the command-result repository bound to the durable persistence provider in the intended composition?
targetedEvidenceQuestions.why: create_execution is already idempotent through the CommandInbox. The receipt path matters for the metadata operations, whose effect idempotency is the injected callback's property.

targetedEvidenceQuestions.question: Where is the LocalProjectGrant issued and validated on the product side, and which Control Plane component is intended to consume it for a direct-local dispatch?
targetedEvidenceQuestions.why: The Control Plane has no grant authority of its own. The answer decides whether the fix is a grant check in the direct drivers or a different composition boundary.
targetedEvidenceQuestions.owner: W1 with the Agent HQ desktop owner

targetedEvidenceQuestions.question: Which component is authoritative for the Local workspace and project authorization set that the private API should compare a request against?
targetedEvidenceQuestions.why: The hosted path compares signed claims. The Local path needs the equivalent authoritative set before the body-derived scope can be replaced.
targetedEvidenceQuestions.owner: W1 (apps/control-api authentication) with the Agent HQ product owner

targetedEvidenceQuestions.question: Which profile is expected to compose a SandboxProvider, and what E2B template, network, resource and cleanup policy is the intended baseline?
targetedEvidenceQuestions.why: Without a composed provider there is no sandbox boundary to accept, and the live E2B gate cannot be closed.
targetedEvidenceQuestions.owner: W1 (profile composition) with the operations owner

targetedEvidenceQuestions.question: Is the value-based SecretCanaryGuard intended to run at every content sink, and what is the authoritative protected-value set?
targetedEvidenceQuestions.why: The production guard exists but has no call site, and the key-name redaction misses compound credential names. The answer decides filter placement and ownership.

targetedEvidenceQuestions.question: Which composition owns the pi-durable data directory, and is it ever created outside an owner-only ancestor?
targetedEvidenceQuestions.why: The adapter inherits the guarantee today. If a profile can point the adapter at a directory that is not inside an owner-only ancestor, the adapter-owned directory becomes a supported traversal path.
targetedEvidenceQuestions.owner: W1 (packages/pi-durable-adapter and the apps/control-api pi-durable composition)
